issue.title: getRequestListener: uncaught `socket.destroySoon is not a function` in forceClose when the socket is mocked (e.g. fastify.inject via MCP SDK)
Header object passed to c.body() is mutated, so reusing it returns 500 from the second request on
On Node 26.11, reading `duplex` on the lightweight request throws `ERR_INVALID_THIS`, so `new Request(url, c.req.raw)` fails
issue.body:
### Versions

- `@hono/node-server` 2.1.5 (also 2.1.4)
- `hono` 4.13.12
- Node **26.11.1** fails (also 26.11.0). Node **26.10.0** works.

### What happens

Any code that passes the request `c.req.raw` from `@hono/node-server` as a `RequestInit` now throws on Node 26.11. A common example is rewriting the URL before handing the request to an auth library:

```js
new Request(new URL('/rewritten', c.req.url), c.req.raw)
```

```
TypeError [ERR_INVALID_THIS]: Illegal invocation
```

Every Better Auth endpoint that is routed through this rewrite returns 500.

### Minimal reproduction

```js
// package.json: { "type": "module", "dependencies": { "@hono/node-server": "2.1.5", "hono": "4.13.12" } }
import { serve } from '@hono/node-server'
import { Hono } from 'hono'

const app = new Hono()
app.all('*', (c) => {
  try {
    const r = new Request(new URL('/rewritten', c.req.url), c.req.raw)
    return c.text(`OK method=${r.method}`)
  } catch (e) {
    return c.text(`FAIL ${e.name} code=${e.code} ${e.message}`, 500)
  }
})

const server = serve({ fetch: app.fetch, port: 0 }, async (info) => {
  const base = `http://127.0.0.1:${info.port}`
  const get = await fetch(`${base}/api/x`)
  const post = await fetch(`${base}/api/x`, { method: 'POST', body: '{"a":1}' })
  console.log(`node ${process.version} | GET: ${get.status} ${await get.text()} | POST: ${post.status} ${await post.text()}`)
  server.close()
})
```

Output (`docker run node:<version>-alpine`):

```
node v26.10.0 | GET: 200 OK method=GET | POST: 200 OK method=POST
node v26.11.1 | GET: 500 FAIL TypeError code=ERR_INVALID_THIS Illegal invocation | POST: 500 FAIL TypeError code=ERR_INVALID_THIS Illegal invocation
```

To find the failing property, I read each `Request` property on `c.req.raw`. On 26.11.1 only one throws:

```
node v26.10.0 | no property throws
node v26.11.1 | throws: duplex(ERR_INVALID_THIS)
```

### Cause

- Node 26.11.0 updated undici to 8.11.2. undici 8.11.0 includes nodejs/undici#5792 ("use private fields for brand checks"). Since then, the getters on `Request.prototype` throw unless `this` is a real undici `Request`.
- The lightweight request in `src/request.ts` forwards a fixed list of properties to the real request through `getRequestCache()`: `cache`, `credentials`, `destination`, `integrity`, `mode`, `redirect`, `referrer`, `referrerPolicy` and `keepalive`. `duplex` is not on that list. Reading `duplex` therefore falls through to undici's own `Request.prototype.duplex` getter, which now fails its brand check.
- The `Request` constructor reads `init.duplex`, so passing the lightweight request as `init` throws.

### Suggested fix

Add `duplex` to the forwarded properties in `src/request.ts`:

```ts
;[
  'cache',
  'credentials',
  'destination',
  'duplex',
  'integrity',
  // ...
```

Two other fixes are possible, depending on what you want to support: forward every remaining `Request.prototype` getter so that a future undici getter can't hit the same problem, or return the constant `'half'`.

### Related

- honojs/hono#5538: the same kind of failure in `bodyLimit` (`new Request(c.req.raw, init)`) with `overrideGlobalObjects: false`.
- nodejs/undici#5792: the brand-check change.

issue.title: Response body returned after client disconnect is never cancelled
A paced streaming response keeps one Promise for each chunk while write() returns true
issue.body:
Hello, and thank you for `@hono/node-server`. We use it for the two Node.js services that stream our web radio.

I would like to report a memory growth that we found on those services, with a reproduction and a possible fix.

### What happens

A streaming response whose source is paced keeps one `Promise` for each chunk it writes, for as long as `write()` returns `true`. Our audio streams do not end and never fill the socket, so the memory of each service grew until a listener disconnected (about 16 MB an hour in production, at about 41 chunks of 400 bytes a second).

I see the same growth with `streamSSE` (one event each millisecond). A source that produces as fast as it can does not show it: `write()` then returns `false` from time to time, and the chain settles.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/Mheaus/hono-node-server-stream-promise-chain

```bash
npm install
npm start            # paced source
PACED=0 npm start    # source as fast as possible
```

The script serves one streaming route with Hono, reads it with `fetch`, and prints the number of live `Promise` objects every 20 000 chunks. It counts them with `v8.queryObjects`, which collects garbage first.

`@hono/node-server` 2.1.4, `hono` 4.12.31, Node.js 24.21.0, macOS arm64:

| Chunks sent | Live `Promise` objects | Heap used |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 20 000 | 20 053 | 9.8 MiB |
| 60 000 | 60 053 | 13.8 MiB |
| 100 000 | 100 053 | 17.8 MiB |

Node.js 20.20.2 and 22.23.3 show the same growth, and so does version 1.19.14. With `PACED=0` the count stays between 105 and 207. The README has every number.

### What I think the cause is

In `writeFromReadableStreamDefaultReader` (`src/utils.ts`), `flow` runs as a `then` callback and returns the promise of the next read:

```ts
} else {
  return reader.read().then(flow, handleStreamError)
}
```

A promise returned from a `then` callback makes the promise of that `then` wait for it ([NewPromiseResolveThenableJob](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-newpromiseresolvethenablejob)). While `write()` returns `true`, each chunk adds one promise to a chain. The chain settles only when the stream ends, when `write()` returns `false`, or on an error.

### A possible fix

Start the next read without returning its promise. As far as I can see, nothing reads the value that `flow` returns, and the errors still reach `handleStreamError`:

```diff
-        return reader.read().then(flow, handleStreamError)
+        reader.read().then(flow, handleStreamError)
```

With this change built into the reproduction, the count stays at 63 from 20 000 to 100 000 chunks.

I read in the contribution guide of Hono that pull requests are for maintainers, so I have not opened one. The change is on a branch of my fork, with a test, in case it saves you time:

https://github.com/honojs/node-server/compare/main...Mheaus:node-server:fix/stream-write-promise-chain

The test counts the live promises while a stream stays open. It fails on `main` with `expected 2000 to be less than 200`. `format`, `lint`, `typecheck` and the tests pass on Node.js 20, 22 and 24. One caveat: the test uses `v8.queryObjects`, which still prints an `ExperimentalWarning` on these versions. I will gladly change the approach or test something else if you prefer.

Thank you for your time.

issue.title: A body failing before its first chunk is sent as a complete, empty 200 when `overrideGlobalObjects` is false
c.req.raw.signal is not triggered with node:http2
v2: body read after client disconnect rejects with `TypeError: Body is unusable` even when the full body was received (regression from v1)
Please document the `COMPRESSIBLE_CONTENT_TYPE_REGEX`-related behavior
issue.body:
In the [serveStatic](https://github.com/honojs/node-server/blob/9e1cdee836baeb13f33e857a582b29546185c324/src/serve-static.ts#L21) middleware, there exists a check for compressible content types (in the `COMPRESSIBLE_CONTENT_TYPE_REGEX`)... if this check fails, then the compressed version of a file will never be served, even IF there does exist a compressed variant of that file!

While experimenting with using [compression for a large binary file in one of my web projects](https://moursy.org/funbox/autoconnections), I found after analysing the network requests that the large file was not being served as a compressed Brotli file like it should have been (thus wasting precious network bandwidth and user time)!

When I saw that other files, like the actual `.html` were being served compressed, I had a hunch something was awry in the `serveStatic` middleware. After peeking the source code, I found that my hunch was correct, and renaming file from `.bin` to `.txt` (although technically incorrect) made Hono start serving the compressed version of the large file!

Considering that this behaviour is undocumented and could lead to user confusion, I ask that you document this somewhere.
